posts.title: Five chat openers that actually get replies
posts.excerpt: Short, specific and human: what to say in the first ten seconds of a conversation.
posts.author: Maya Ortiz
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • Openers that reference the page beat generic greetings.
  • Offer one specific thing rather than "let me know if you need help".
  • Ask a narrow question that is easy to answer in one word.
  • Stay quiet where visitors are mid-task, such as payment steps.

Why the first message matters

Visitors decide in seconds whether a chat bubble is worth their attention. A vague greeting reads like a template, and templates get ignored.

A good opener shows you noticed where they are and makes replying feel effortless.

1. Reference the page they are on

If someone is reading a shipping policy, ask about shipping. It proves the message is for them, not for everyone.

Try: "Comparing delivery options? I can tell you what arrives before Friday."

2. Offer one specific thing

Replace "How can I help?" with a concrete offer: a size guide, a quote, a five-minute setup call.

Specific offers are easier to accept because the visitor knows what happens next.

3. Ask a narrow question

Open questions require effort. Closed or two-choice questions get answers.

"Are you shopping for yourself or for a gift?"
An example that works on most product pages

4. Put a human name on it

A first name and a recognisable avatar make the chat feel like a person, even when the AI agent answers first.

5. Know when to stay quiet

Do not interrupt checkout or a form the visitor is filling out. Trigger proactive messages on browsing pages, or after a short period of inactivity.

Weak openerStronger opener
"Hi, need help?""Want a hand choosing a size?"
"Ask us anything!""Curious about delivery to your area?"

Frequently asked questions

Start with two or three, one per page type, and compare reply rates.

Yes for common pages, with a clear path to a person.

Yes. Match the visitor's language when you can.

posts.title: Introducing smarter handoffs
posts.excerpt: The AI agent now knows when to step aside, and who to pass the conversation to.
posts.author: Daniel Reyes
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • The agent detects when a conversation needs judgment and routes it.
  • The full transcript, intent and customer details travel with the handoff.
  • You choose the rules: by topic, language, plan or sentiment.

What is new

Until now, handoffs were a single fallback. Now the agent decides who should take over, and why, before it says goodbye to the customer.

How it decides

The agent looks at three signals:

  • Confidence in the answer it can give from your sources.
  • Topic, such as billing disputes or cancellations.
  • Sentiment, when a customer is clearly frustrated.

What the human receives

A short summary, the customer's history, and the exact question that could not be answered. Nobody has to ask "what happened so far?"

Set it up in three steps

  1. Open the AI agent settings and choose Handoff rules.
  2. Pick a topic or condition and the team that should receive it.
  3. Test in the playground, then publish.
Tip: start with billing and cancellations, which usually need a person.

Frequently asked questions

Yes, at any time.

The agent collects details and creates a ticket for the next available teammate.

It is included on all plans that include the AI agent.

posts.title: What a fast first reply is really worth
posts.excerpt: We compared response time against conversion across a sample of stores.
posts.author: Priya Nair
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • In our sample data, faster first replies were linked with higher conversion.
  • The biggest jump came from getting under one minute.
  • AI can cover the gap outside working hours.
  • Figures here are illustrative for this demo site.

What we looked at

We grouped chats by how quickly the first reply arrived and compared how many led to a purchase or booking.

Correlation is not causation, so treat this as a direction rather than a promise.

What stood out

< 1 minhighest conversion band
1–5 minmoderate drop-off
> 30 minmost chats went cold

The pattern held across store sizes, with the steepest change in the first minute.

How to reply faster

  • Let the AI agent answer common questions instantly.
  • Use canned replies for the next ten.
  • Route chats by topic so the right person sees them first.
  • Set clear business hours and an honest offline message.

Caveats

Speed helps only if the answer is good. A fast wrong answer is worse than a slightly slower right one.

Frequently asked questions

Under one minute for chat is a sensible goal.

Yes, if it actually answers the question.

Use the analytics report for first response time per channel.

posts.title: Build a help center your bot can lean on
posts.excerpt: Write each answer once and let it serve customers and the AI agent alike.
posts.author: Maya Ortiz
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • One clear article per question beats many overlapping ones.
  • Lead with the answer, then explain the exceptions.
  • Review what the agent could not answer and fill the gaps weekly.

Why articles matter for AI

An AI agent is only as good as the sources behind it. Clear, current articles produce clear, current answers.

Structure each article

  1. State the question as a customer would ask it.
  2. Answer in the first two sentences.
  3. List exceptions and edge cases.
  4. Link to the next step.

Find the gaps

Open the unanswered-questions report each week. Every question the agent handed off is a candidate for a new article.

Tip: write the article, then re-ask the same question in the playground to check it works.

Keep it fresh

Assign an owner to every article and review policies whenever they change. Outdated answers are the fastest way to lose trust.

Frequently asked questions

Start with your top twenty questions and grow from there.

As short as the answer allows.

Yes, connect documents as additional sources.

posts.title: How we run support across six time zones
posts.excerpt: Rotas, handoff notes and the habits that keep replies quick.
posts.author: Daniel Reyes
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • Follow-the-sun rotas keep coverage without night shifts.
  • Written handoff notes matter more than meetings.
  • The AI agent covers the gaps between shifts.

Design the rota

We split the day into overlapping regional shifts so there is always someone awake and a fifteen-minute overlap for handoffs.

Write good handoff notes

  • Open conversations and their status.
  • Anything promised to a customer.
  • Known incidents.

Let the agent cover the edges

Between shifts the AI agent answers common questions and creates tickets with full context for the next region.

Protect the team

Rotate hard shifts fairly and keep response-time goals realistic.

“Good coverage should never depend on one person staying up.”
Daniel Reyes

Frequently asked questions

Enough to cover peak hours in each region, with the agent handling the rest.

Yes, one inbox with regional views.

posts.title: Routing rules, explained
posts.excerpt: Send the right chat to the right person without a maze of rules.
posts.author: Priya Nair
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • Start with three rules: language, topic and plan.
  • Order matters: the first matching rule wins.
  • Always keep a catch-all so nothing waits unassigned.

How rules work

Each rule has a condition and an action. When a new conversation arrives, Loop checks rules from top to bottom and applies the first match.

Rules worth having

ConditionAction
Language is SpanishAssign to Spanish team
Topic is billingAssign to finance
Plan is premiumMark high priority

Avoid the maze

More rules are not better rules. Merge overlapping ones, and review them monthly.

Keep a catch-all rule at the bottom.

Frequently asked questions

Yes, the agent can tag the intent that rules match on.

Chats queue for the team and the agent collects details.

posts.title: Hiring your first support agent
posts.excerpt: What to look for, and how to set them up to succeed.
posts.author: Maya Ortiz
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • Hire for empathy and clear writing before product knowledge.
  • Give them a playbook and a shadowing week.
  • Let the AI agent take the repetitive load from day one.

What to look for

Clear writing, calm under pressure and curiosity. Product details can be taught in a week.

Onboard in a week

  1. Day 1: read the help center and past chats.
  2. Days 2–3: shadow live conversations.
  3. Days 4–5: reply with review.

Give them good tools

Canned replies, a shared inbox and clear routing make the first month far easier.

Frequently asked questions

Part-time plus the AI agent is a common starting point.

posts.title: Which customer questions can AI answer today?
posts.excerpt: A look at the question types that resolve without a person, in our sample data.
posts.author: Priya Nair
posts.body:
Key takeaways
  • Order status, policies and how-to questions resolve most often.
  • Emotional or high-stakes topics belong with people.
  • Figures are illustrative for this demo site.

Easy wins

Order statusresolves most often
Policiesvery high
How-tohigh

Where humans stay involved

Complaints, refunds with exceptions and anything emotional deserve a person, with the agent handing over context.

How to raise the rate

  • Fill gaps in your help center.
  • Connect order data.
  • Review handoffs weekly.

Frequently asked questions

Not desirable. Aim for the right questions, not all questions.
